project: Additive CI Classifier and Focused Verification Targets
description: Replace the four-outcome exclusive CI classifier with deterministic additive verification-lane outputs derived from changed-path ownership, and add focused root Make verification targets so each lane can run only its owned scope. Factory-content-only changes select no lanes, mixed changes select exact unions, and CI/tooling or unknown paths conservatively select every lane, while workflow routing remains unchanged for the dependent project.

context.customerAsk: Rewrite cmd/ciclassify to emit additive path-ownership lane decisions, cover the governing plan's nine-case validation matrix with exact emitted-lane assertions, and add focused root Make verification targets including a narrow real-backend UI integration target. Keep Makefile changes limited to new targets, reconcile concurrent Makefile work through the mandatory contention protocol, and do not add job-level workflow routing in this lane.
context.problem: The existing four-outcome exclusive classifier cannot express exact verification unions for mixed changes, so pull requests pay runner-queue and wall-clock costs for unrelated jobs. Broad Make entry points also combine independently owned checks, while an incomplete ownership policy could allow unknown paths to escape required verification.
context.solution: Expose one focused root Make rerun command per verification lane, with UI-backend integration limited to browser tests that start or call a real backend; classify normalized changed paths through an explicit ownership policy; union all matched lanes; treat factory content as neutral; select every lane for empty, tooling, Go-toolchain, or unknown input; and prove the contract with exact table-driven fixtures for all nine governing validation cases without editing CI workflows.

acceptanceCriteria: The root Makefile exposes a direct focused rerun command for every classifier lane; each command runs only its owned scope, and the UI-backend integration command runs real-backend browser coverage without Storybook-only checks.
cmd/ciclassify emits named Boolean lane outputs from changed-path ownership, selects exact unions for mixed inputs, and produces deterministic decisions independent of input order or duplicate paths.
factory/**-only input selects no verification lanes; factory content combined with an owned product path does not add or suppress that product path's lanes.
Empty input, .github/workflows/**, CI scripts, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, and unknown paths select every verification lane conservatively.

Table-driven unit fixtures reproduce all nine cases in the governing validation matrix, with each case asserting the complete emitted lane set, and no .github/workflows/** file changes in this project.
Typecheck and focused tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file contention are resolved against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Run core product verification through focused commands
userStories.description: As a CI maintainer, I want separate frontend, backend, and UI-backend integration commands so a selected product lane can be rerun without invoking unrelated verification.
acceptanceCriteria: A direct root Make command runs the complete frontend-owned scope: typecheck, frontend lint, frontend unit/coverage, browser verification, and applicable public UI-package verification, without backend verification.
A direct root Make command runs the backend-owned scope: backend build plus required backend unit and functional verification, without frontend coverage.
make ui-backend-integration runs only browser integration that starts or calls a real backend and proves a browser request against it; it does not run Storybook-only checks.
Existing broader verification commands retain their observable scope and can compose the focused commands without duplicating a selected check.
Makefile changes are scoped to new focused targets and their declarations; concurrent unit, functional, and lint target mechanics are preserved after rebasing onto current main.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added explicit root frontend-verification, backend-verification, and ui-backend-integration targets that compose existing checks without changing broader verification mechanics. The frontend lane covers typecheck, lint, component/unit coverage, browser and Storybook checks, and public UI-package verification without backend checks; the backend lane covers build plus unit and functional coverage; the integration lane is limited to the real-backend durable-session browser suite. Updated classifier rerun commands to emit these direct targets. Verified with make -n for all three targets, go test ./cmd/ciclassify -count=1, make typecheck, make ui-lint, make test, and git diff --check.

userStories.title: Run supporting verification lanes through focused commands
userStories.description: As a CI maintainer, I want one local command per documentation, package-family, and local-inference lane so future routing can select package self-verification and specialty checks independently.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation reference and root README lanes resolve to the existing focused make docs-reference-smoke and make readme-check behavior.

API Package, Packaged Factories Package, and Model Providers Package each resolve to a direct root Make command that runs that package family's self-verification; required backend or frontend consumer verification remains a separate classifier lane rather than being hidden inside package self-verification.
The Local Inference lane resolves to one Linux-capable focused Make command that executes the managed-runtime and real-inference regression once, with no duplicate real-inference invocation.
Every supporting lane has one documented direct local rerun command that can be emitted by the classifier.
Existing package publication policy and protected-main candidate prerequisites are unchanged.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Kept docs-reference-smoke, readme-check, api-package-verify, packaged-factory-package-verify, and model-provider-package-verify as the direct supporting-lane rerun commands. Added local-inference-verification, which composes long-tests-managed-runtime and exactly one pr-inference-approval execution without the broader specialty sweep, and updated classifier output to emit that command. Verified all five supporting commands, the managed-runtime regression, make -n command expansion, go test ./cmd/ciclassify -count=1, and make typecheck; the real-inference executable is Linux/runner-gated and was not available in this Windows worktree.

userStories.title: Emit additive path-ownership lane decisions
userStories.description: As a pull-request contributor, I want changed paths to select the exact union of relevant verification lanes so my change receives complete but non-duplicative verification and unfamiliar changes remain safe.
acceptanceCriteria: The classifier emits named Boolean decisions and focused rerun commands for Documentation Reference, README, Frontend, Backend, UI Backend Integration, API Package, Packaged Factories Package, Model Providers Package, and Local Inference lanes.

Path ownership follows the governing classification contract, including API and generated contract surfaces, backend/CLI surfaces, each package family and its scripts, local-inference surfaces, docs, README, frontend, factory content, CI/tooling, and unknown paths.
Mixed paths select the set union of owned lanes; duplicate paths and changed-path input order do not alter the emitted decisions.
factory/**-only input emits every lane as false, while factory content mixed with another owned path yields exactly the other path's lanes.
Empty input, workflow or CI-script paths, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, and an unknown root path emit every lane as true.

Table-driven fixtures cover the nine validation-matrix cases exactly: factory only; reference docs; root README; frontend; backend or CLI; API contract; each package family independently; mixed frontend/backend; and conservative full verification inputs. Each case asserts the complete emitted lane set.
Classifier summaries and GitHub-compatible outputs report the same lane decisions and remain usable by the later routing project, but no workflow consumes them in this project.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
